about: The Connecticut Shade blend in the three core LH lines from Nicholas Syris, rolled in Costa Rica. The names Claro, Colorado and Maduro refer to wrapper shade.
notes: Two versions exist. The current Claro was reblended to be a milder, traditional Connecticut. The stronger original, with the black and gold band, came back in 2018 in Robusto, Toro and Gordo. No reviewer or maker strength rating was found.
verifyNotes: Wrapper, binder, filler, factory, sizes and 2014 debut confirmed on halfwheel. about: The Ecuadorian Habano blend in the three core LH lines from Nicholas Syris, rolled at Tabacos de Costa Rica. It was the third LH blend to reach the U.S., debuting at the 2015 trade show.
notes: Strength and body are from Cigar Coop's review; halfwheel found it below medium for most of the smoke. Cigar Coop lists the filler as Brazil, Nicaragua and Peru instead of Ecuador, Peru and Nicaragua.

about: The maduro blend in the three core LH lines from Nicholas Syris, using an Ecuadorian Criollo maduro wrapper and rolled in Costa Rica. It came to the U.S. with the Claro in 2014.
notes: Strength, body and flavors are from Cigar Coop's reviews. Cigar Coop lists the filler as Nicaragua, Peru and Brazil, and in 2019 called the wrapper Ecuadorian Habano Maduro.

about: A 6 x 52 toro from LH Cigars that was first made for private clients outside the U.S. and came to the American market in 2020. It wears the original black and gold LH band.
notes: Also called Lavida Habana LE. Binder and filler are undisclosed. 2020 is the U.S. launch; it was sold abroad for years before. Strength and body are from Cigar Coop's review.
verifyNotes: All fields confirmed. Notes trimmed slightly.

about: A line named for LH Cigars founder Nicholas Syris that grew out of the Nick & Jim P.B.E. collaboration. It began as a lonsdale made for 2nd Street Cigars and went national in 2020 with the Panzon figurado.
notes: Strength, body and flavors are from Cigar Coop's Panzon review, which found it building to medium-full in the last third. The Nick Sofos salomon carries the Nick name but is a different blend.

about: A blend from LH Cigars named with the Greek form of Nick, after founder Nicholas Syris' Greek roots. The company made it as a stronger, bolder option than its other cigars.
notes: The maker calls it stronger and fuller bodied than its other blends, but no rating was found. Cigar Coop treats it as part of the Nick line. Launched in one size with more promised.

about: A 6 x 58 short salomon from LH Cigars, named with the Greek word for wise as a nod to founder Nicholas Syris' heritage. It is sold under the Nick name but uses its own blend.
notes: An extension of the Nick line in one size, with a different blend from the other Nick cigars. Strength, body and flavors are from Cigar Coop's review.

about: The first LH Cigars blend with a Mexican San Andres wrapper, released in 2024 as part of the Nick family. It is made at Tabacos de Costa Rica in two sizes.
notes: halfwheel reports 10,000 robustos and 25,000 toros made; Cigar Coop calls it a limited production line. Strength, body and flavors are from Cigar Coop's review.

about: A limited cigar marking ten years of LH Cigars in the U.S. market, made at Tabacos de Costa Rica. Its 5 7/8 x 52 size is a tribute to the Cohiba Siglo VI.
notes: Binder and filler are undisclosed, and the production number was not released. halfwheel rated strength mild with medium body; Cigar Coop rated both medium.
